newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Weak franc, money rate rise to dog Belgian OLOs.
newsitem.headline: Weak franc, money rate rise to dog Belgian OLOs.

text.p: Belgian government bonds (OLOs) and futures will continue to be dogged by a weak franc and high money rates, while waiting for relief, dealers said on Friday.

Help ought to come from the Bundesbank, which, dealers speculate, could be getting concerned by the mark's soft tone vis a vis the dollar. The weighty U.S. currency is pressuring not only the mark, but also units in the mark bloc.

Market hopes centre mainly on verbal intervention by the German central bank, although there are some hopes for a rise in either key rates or the repo rate. "But raising German rates would run counter to all (weak) fundamentals," a trader said.

In the absence of German moves the Belgian National Bank will likely keep local liquidity low to give indirect support to the franc. The franc was at 20.6470/85 to the mark at 1505 GMT, unchanged from late Thursday levels.
One trader said OLOs faced a "more structural" problem in that short Belgian rates were above their German equivalents, making funding OLO positions relatively expensive.

He said the market was also suffering somewhat from funds selling out of OLOs and moving into other European bonds as part of pre-EMU adjustments of their portfolios."They are Europeanising their holdings," he said.
He noted players could swap OLOs for Bunds without giving up too much in terms of yields.
Technically, the market was ready for curve steepening -- covering shorts at the short end -- after the recent outburst of flattening trades, but he doubted this would happen.
OLOs and OLO futures were back at or even below week-ago levels, paring the gains posted on the back of hopes U.S. interest rates would hold steady for now.
Prices slipped in nervous, lively trade, weighed down by concerns European rates might have to rise to fight off possible inflationary pressure from a runaway dollar.
The rate rise fears are compounded by expectations of an expected upturn to European economies later in the second half.
"Rate fears are dragging money rates up and the short end down, which is dragging the long end down," a trader said.
At 4.05/15 one-week repo rates rose above four percent, up from 3.90/00 late on Thursday. The rise removed any interest in maturities up to 1999 with yields below four percent.

"There was selling over the whole of the curve. For the first time at the long end too," a trader said. But while short yields have risen by some 20 bps over the past week, maturities beyond 2004 have held relatively steady.
Traders reported concern the Bundesbank would act sooner rather than later to prop up a weakening mark, and indirectly the closely-linked franc.

Speculation centres on the Bundesbank repo rate which the German central bank on Thursday fixed for two weeks at an unchanged 3.00 percent. But dealers noted the Bundesbank did not nail down the rate at that level for the whole of the four-week period when its policy-making council does not meet.
That left room for the bank to raise the rate outright, probably by a quarter point, or to revert to a floating rate, which would effectively lead to a rate rise too, dealers said.
Dealers said the Belgian central bank would follow a Bundesbank move by raising its central rate, currently at 3.00 percent. The increase would most likely be by a quarter point.

Benchmark 10-year OLOs underperformed Bunds, though, which suffered from profit-taking after recent hefty gains. However, any major sell-off should be seen as a buying opportunity, German traders said.
The 10-year OLO/Bund yield spread MEUR widened to nine basis points from seven in morning trade and eight late on Thursday.
-- Nieck Ammerlaan, Brussels Newsroom +32 2 287 6816, Fax +32 2 230 7710
